interpretation.objective: For each tram line option under public discussion in Tallinn, route the line along the real street network, model its stops, and measure who and what would be within walking distance: residents (and those not yet near a tram), workplaces, public services and development in preparation. Set this beside the line's standing in the city's strategies and plans, and rank the options under several declared weightings.

assumptions.statement: The options are the 28 alignments in scenarios/tram-options.yaml: the 13 lines and variants discussed in city documents and news between 2019 and November 2026, and 15 further corridors of the 2019 feasibility and cost-benefit study, among them the corridors that leave Tallinn (Peetri and Assaku, Jüri, Tabasalu and its extension, Maardu, and the Viimsi line to Haabneeme). Not compared as options, but shown on the map by stage (A12): the study's railway services (Balti jaam – Vesse, the Bekkeri branch), connecting links under 1 km (the airport – Lubja tunnel link 5C, the Rahu tee – Laagna tee link 3A+) and the loop inside Mustamäe drawn with corridor 7A. Corridors the study itself dropped (Paljassaare, Veerenni, Tondi, Mustamäe tee) are in neither.
assumptions.rationale: The study plans a network for Tallinn and Harju county, and its first stage already leaves the city. Buildings of the municipalities around Tallinn come from the national copy of the same building layer (A13), so a line outside the city is measured on the same basis for residents and workplaces.

assumptions.statement: A place is within reach of a stop when the walk along the path network is at most 500 m (about 6 minutes at 4.8 km/h), including the straight-line gaps between the building or stop and the nearest path. Distances of 300, 400, 600 and 800 m are also computed.
assumptions.rationale: 400-500 m is the usual planning catchment of a tram stop; the Tallinn 2035 strategy uses 400 m. The other distances let the reader test the sensitivity.

assumptions.statement: Stops of a proposed line are modelled every 500 m along it, with a stop at each end. A modelled stop within 80 m of an existing tram stop is treated as that stop.
assumptions.rationale: Stop locations are published for almost none of the options. 500 m is close to the spacing of the existing network. Modelled stops are not planned stop locations.

assumptions.statement: Each line is the shortest path between its declared waypoints over the street network, with streets the option does not name costing 8 times their length. Where the described corridor has no street (the Putukaväil corridor, the planned Rahu tee) a named stand-in street or the city's published corridor drawing is used, and the option says so. The fifteen corridors added from the 2019 study, like the Rahu tee line, are taken from the city's published drawing of the study corridors, between named ends of its lines, and are not routed on the street network.
assumptions.rationale: The sources describe alignments by street names, not coordinates. Routing by name on real geometry avoids hand-drawn lines and can be checked against the corridors the city has published.

assumptions.statement: Residents per building are estimated: the population of each Statistics Estonia 1 km grid cell (2024) is shared among the existing registered dwellings in the cell in proportion to their net floor area. Buildings cover the whole frame, so a cell on the city boundary is shared between the dwellings on both sides of it.
assumptions.rationale: No open dataset gives residents per building. The grid fixes the totals per square kilometre; registered dwelling floor area is the best open proxy inside a cell.

assumptions.statement: Workplaces and destinations are measured as the net floor area of existing registered non-residential buildings: hospitality, offices, retail and services, transport and communication buildings, industry and warehouses, and public buildings. Garages and outbuildings are not counted. Floor area is a proxy, not a count of jobs.
assumptions.rationale: No open dataset gives jobs at building or block level in Tallinn.

assumptions.statement: Development in preparation is measured two ways: the floor area of registered dwellings that are planned or under construction, and the area of detailed plans in process (initiated, adopted for display or applied for) inside the drawn catchment. The growth criterion is the average of the two, each relative to the best option. Planned buildings are measured in and around Tallinn; detailed plans in process are those of the Tallinn planning register only.
assumptions.rationale: Neither measure is a forecast of new residents. Planned buildings appear in the layer only once they have a footprint; a plan in process says where development is being prepared, not how much.

assumptions.statement: The score is a weighted sum of seven criteria, each expressed as the option's value divided by the best option's value: residents newly in reach, all residents in reach, workplace floor area, public services, growth, residents in reach per km of new track, and strategy fit. The accepted weighting is 'balanced' (20, 10, 15, 10, 15, 15, 15 %); four other weightings are published.
assumptions.rationale: The question asks to consider population, services, strategies and plans together; any single ranking needs weights. The weights are a judgement, so the alternatives are computed by the pipeline and shown next to the accepted one.

assumptions.statement: Strategy fit (0-3) is the sum of three scores of 0-1 recorded per option with their sources: its place in the mobility plan SUMP 2035, its stage in the 2019 feasibility study, and the city government's position in 2026. The study stage is read from the city's drawing of the study corridors, because the report shows the stages on maps only.
assumptions.rationale: Strategies and political decisions are documents, not geodata. A fixed rubric applied to every option, with the evidence listed, keeps the judgement inspectable.

assumptions.statement: Published costs and ridership are quoted per option for reference and are not part of the score.
assumptions.rationale: The estimates come from different years (2019 to 2026), price levels and alignments, and are missing for some options.

assumptions.statement: The 2019 study's own results are quoted per option and are not part of the score: stage, infrastructure cost, and the benefit-cost ratio and net present value of the tram variant in its four scenarios (final report, Tables 45, 61 and 62). Tables show the ratio for 'Tallinn++ with free public transport'.
assumptions.rationale: The study measures something this model does not (travel time, traffic, environmental and health effects from a transport model), for corridors that do not always match an option's extent. Putting its ratio in the score would mix two methods and count 2019 assumptions as current. Tallinn++ is the scenario the study recommends, and its authors advise comparing on the free-public-transport runs.

assumptions.statement: The five development stages of the 2019 study (report chapter 1.6) are shown in full: every line of the city's drawing of the study corridors, in and outside Tallinn, grouped by stage and named with the corridor code printed on the report's maps (scenarios/study-2019-stages.yaml). A study corridor counts as compared when at least half of it lies within 75 m of an option. The stage layer itself takes no part in the score; the options that stand for its corridors do.
assumptions.rationale: The study plans a network for Tallinn and Harju county, and its first stage already leaves the city (Peetri and Assaku). Showing only the options would hide the stage each belongs to and the corridors that are not compared.

assumptions.statement: Outside Tallinn, residents, workplaces and planned buildings are measured from the national layer of ETAK building footprints with Building Register attributes, of which the city's layer is a copy; inside the city the city's copy is used and a building is never counted from both. Public services and detailed plans in process are the city's own layers and are counted in Tallinn only. The existing tram network is compared with Tallinn's population. The frame reaches at least 2 km beyond every study corridor.
assumptions.rationale: The two building layers have the same origin and fields and agree on status and use for over 99.8 % of the buildings in Tallinn, so the residents and workplace criteria are comparable across the boundary. No open layer of services or plans in process covers the neighbouring municipalities on the city's definitions; counting them in Tallinn only understates a line outside the city on two criteria, which is reported per option rather than hidden.

tram = route_type 900; weekday = services running on Wednesdays and valid on the latest calendar start date

steps.verify: every waypoint must resolve in the immutable sources and at least 70 % of the routed line must follow the declared streets, else the option is rejected

one feature per corridor of the 2019 study, from the lines of the city's drawing named for it; stage, share of length inside Tallinn, and the options within 75 m of at least half of it
steps.verify: every line of the drawing is named exactly once, in the stage the drawing gives it; the drawn length of each stage is within 6 % of the report's total

steps.distance_basis: building centroid or service point to nearest routing node (straight line) plus network distance to the nearest stop

steps.expression: score = 100 x sum(weight x value / best value) over seven criteria, per weighting profile and walking distance

warnings.statement: Every proposed line is a modelled reading of public descriptions, routed along the street network. It is not a designed track alignment, and the stops, placed every 500 m, are not planned stops. Results near the ends of a line and for short lines depend most on these choices.
warnings.mitigation: Use the results to compare corridors, not to judge a design. Replace an option with surveyed design geometry in data/overrides when it is published.

warnings.statement: Fifteen options are corridors of the 2019 study taken from the city's drawing of them, a schematic line that was not checked against the street network. The 2019 benefit-cost figures shown per option are quoted, refer to the study's corridors (which may be longer than the option or shared by several options) and to 2019 assumptions. The Jüri, Tabasalu and Maardu options continue lines that are not built and are measured on their own.
warnings.mitigation: Read each option's note on the study figures.

warnings.statement: The ranking depends on the weights and on which criteria are included. Longer lines reach more people in total; the per-kilometre criterion only partly offsets that. Ridership, travel time, construction cost and traffic effects are not modelled.
warnings.mitigation: Compare the five published weightings and read the indicators themselves; do not treat one score as a cost-benefit result.

warnings.statement: Residents per building are estimated from the 2024 1 km population grid and registered dwelling floor area. Totals per grid cell are official; the split inside a cell is a model. Workplace floor area is a proxy for jobs and visitors, not a count.
warnings.mitigation: Read differences between options of a few hundred residents as ties.

warnings.statement: Strategy fit is a rubric applied by the analyst to documents and news up to 24 November 2026. Political positions change; the Liivalaia and Pelguranna decisions both changed within the last year.
warnings.mitigation: Check the evidence listed for each option and update scenarios/tram-options.yaml when a decision changes.

warnings.statement: Planned and under-construction buildings are in the layer only when they already have a footprint in the topographic database, and detailed plans in process carry no dwelling numbers. Large future districts such as the former Kopli goods station are therefore under-represented.
warnings.mitigation: Treat the growth criterion as indicative; add planned capacities from the comprehensive plans when they are published as data.

warnings.statement: The Tallinn city ArcGIS services and the GTFS feed do not publish explicit licence text for these layers. The national building layer carries the Maa- ja Ruumiamet open data licence.
warnings.mitigation: Confirm reuse terms with Tallinn City Government before redistributing the source snapshots.

warnings.statement: Population refers to 2024; buildings, plans, services, timetables and the street network to November 2026. Homes completed after 2024 carry too few residents.
warnings.mitigation: Rerun when Statistics Estonia publishes a newer grid.

warnings.statement: Six options leave Tallinn. Residents, workplaces and planned buildings are measured outside the city from the national building layer, but public services and detailed plans in process are the city's own layers and are counted in Tallinn only. For those options the services criterion (10 % of the balanced score) and half of the growth criterion (7.5 %) are a lower bound. Bus departures come from the Tallinn timetable feed only.
warnings.mitigation: Compare the options beyond Tallinn on residents, workplaces and residents per km; the share of each line inside Tallinn is in the tables (length_in_tallinn_pct). Add service and plan layers of Viimsi, Rae, Harku, Jõelähtme and Maardu to score them fully.
